The patient presents with acute-onset, worsening medial knee pain localized to the medial tibia just below the patella, following repetitive pivoting/twisting activity (volleyball). There are no signs of inflammation (no swelling, redness, warmth) or mechanical instability (no weight-bearing difficulty). The diagnostic reasoning explicitly rules out alternatives—e.g., meniscal tear (no locking/giving-way), ligamentous injury (no instability or trauma with deformity), septic/inflammatory arthritis (no fever, effusion, systemic symptoms), or stress fracture (no night pain, no radiographic abnormality).
